component.name: Bible
component.summary: Read, compare and study the Bible offline

description.p: An offline Bible study app for GNOME. Download Bibles, commentaries and books from SWORD repositories once, then read without a connection.

ul.li: Read versions side by side
Highlight verses in named colours
Keep notes as plain Markdown files that work with Obsidian
See the commentary for the verse you are reading
Follow the church year on the Today page
Study the Greek and Hebrew word by word, with a lexicon
Read books, dictionaries and daily devotionals
Explore every cross-reference as a zoomable rainbow, ordered by date, writer, language, genre and more
See places on maps and events on a timeline, with Wikipedia introductions to every book
Listen to chapters, follow reading plans, and keep fasts and feasts
Choose your loading animation: a turning cross, a Chi-Rho, an ichthys or a Trinity knot, used wherever the app waits
Search suggests searches to try
More church-history dates, so Today always has one
A larger test suite
Introductions for the 18 deuterocanonical books (Apocrypha), built in, with their full Wikipedia articles to download
Gentler Wikipedia downloads that use standard picture sizes, to avoid rate limits
A large spinner in the middle of the cross-reference map while it draws
Wikipedia downloads go gently and retry when rate-limited, and say why any failed
Preferences → Book introductions lists every book to download, update or remove one by one
New startup sound: the opening of a Gregorian Kyrie, sung
Cross-references no longer freeze the app: drawing happens in the background with a spinner
Reset view (and Esc), a Read button for the selected passage, a colour legend and a slide-in explanations panel
Intro in the verse dropdown
Full Wikipedia articles with pictures for book introductions, saved for offline reading
Classic typography changes only the text, not the page background
Fixed a crash when playing downloaded audio; playback now uses its own GStreamer player
A log file, with “Open log folder” in Preferences
Audio shows in GNOME’s media controls, with cover art
Over 340,000 built-in cross-references, so the rainbow works with every Bible
Cross-references: zoom down to single verses, see every link meeting at one verse, and experimental circle and matrix views
Order the books by events, age written, writers, language, culture, genre, literary form (songs, parables, prayers…), Hebrew Bible order and more, with explanations on hover
The Today screen is now tiled
Optional two-second startup sound: Old Hundredth, Amazing Grace, Holy Holy Holy or a bell, synthesised from public-domain tunes, with a preview button
Chapter audio: download a chapter or a whole book and listen as you read
Reading plans, with today's reading on the Today page
A passage of the day, today in church history, and what is happening in the chapter you are reading
Introductions to every book, with a map of its places, built in
Bookmarks with tags, and Markdown export
Word study for any Greek or Hebrew word
The cross-reference rainbow
Presentation mode, a verse picker and GNOME Shell search
Optional fasting calendar, classic typography and splash screen

description.p: The Library recommends the Bible that turns on the most features, and lists what each Bible supports: Strong's words, grammar, footnotes, cross-references, red letters and headings.

ul.li: Timeline of biblical history, the kings of Israel and Judah, prophets, who was in power, world events and church history
Every chapter shows when it happened, linked to the timeline
Map of the places named in each chapter, on real geography
Footnotes and cross-references in the Bible text open in place
A "Most popular" group when browsing the library

description.p: Interlinear Greek and Hebrew with a lexicon, dictionaries, books and daily devotionals.
